field_reference_role: Edit target and geometry blueprint, decoded from the original ROM-facing map binaries. Reference PNGs are retained in references/.
field_common_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: actual playable 512x512 SNES RPG field background, a single complete square map.
Input image: EDIT TARGET AND EXACT GEOMETRY BLUEPRINT. Transform its visual rendering into a gorgeous prerendered 3D environment in the mid-1990s style of Super Mario RPG and Final Fantasy VII field backgrounds: chunky modeled diorama objects, richly shaded materials, baked ambient occlusion and soft directional shadows, carefully lit dimensional forms. This is a ground map viewed from a FIXED HIGH OBLIQUE overhead camera, NO SKY, NO HORIZON, no perspective convergence.
ABSOLUTE INVARIANTS: match every path, coastline, impassable forest footprint, building footprint, rock, well, door, bridge and exit in the reference at the EXACT SAME image coordinates and scale. Preserve all open ground. Do not add new solid obstacles, do not remove obstacles, do not move or widen paths, do not change composition or rotate the map. Camera projection must match the reference: vertical screen paths remain vertical and horizontal paths remain horizontal. Ground covers all image edges. The picture must work when a game character walks over the original reference’s collision map.
Render surfaces with smooth readable color masses and chunky volume, no tiny noisy texture or photorealistic grass noise. Trees should become lush overlapping sculpted crowns within their existing silhouette; buildings keep their small existing footprints. Strong warm highlights and blue-violet ambient shadows, night scene but readable. No characters, labels, lettering, grid, borders, HUD or watermark. Render only the environment, edge to edge. Preserve the exact screen-space layout above all else.
Scene:

Solid forest regions are deep sculpted multilayer emerald canopies; the exact branching clearing and winding trails in the image must remain fully walkable and in place. Render large bulbous tropical crowns with rich blue-green highlights, root-edged paths, the reference mushrooms and well. Cyan moonlight and warm amber mushroom accents.

Pale blue-lavender salt floor with restrained large polygonal cracks and rose-purple highlights, sculpted diorama style.

battle_atlas_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production background atlas for an actual 16-bit SNES JRPG.
Create ONE seamless contact sheet of SIX distinct prerendered 3D battle environments, arranged in an exact 2-column by 3-row grid. The canvas is 1536 x 1536; each of the six panels is precisely 768 x 512. No gutters, no borders, no frames, no text, no UI, no characters or creatures. Each panel must fill its rectangular cell edge to edge.
Style: gorgeous mid-1990s Silicon Graphics prerendered game art, the sculpted dimensional miniature sets of Donkey Kong Country and Super Mario RPG. Chunky rounded modeled forms, waxy foliage highlights, tactile bark and stone, baked soft shadows, dramatic colored bounce light, crisp silhouettes. NOT flat pixel art; render fully modeled 3D and it will be downsampled to SNES pixels later.
Camera and composition for EACH panel: landscape side-view JRPG battle stage with slightly elevated camera; horizon about 52 percent down. Bottom 40 percent is a gently textured broad WALKABLE GROUND PLANE, subdued and uncluttered so characters can be composited on it. Keep the central 70 percent of each arena open. Frame with rich large scenery at outer edges, middle-ground architecture and distant atmospheric silhouettes. All scenes at night with clear readable illuminated surfaces, rich saturated jewel colors and warm accents. Avoid near-black crushed shadows.
Panel row 1, column 1: Kampung Sahur, a warm Indonesian village at midnight. Carved timber stilt houses with curved terracotta roofs and glowing amber windows along the back, distant blue mountains and a luminous round moon, tropical banana leaves framing upper corners. Sandy cobblestone clearing with broad warm pools of lantern light.
Panel row 1, column 2: Hutan, an enchanted dense tropical jungle. Massive twisting tree trunks at edges, lush layered emerald broadleaf canopies, mossy exposed roots along the back, cyan shafts of moonlight, little amber bioluminescent mushrooms at the sides. Open velvety moss clearing on bottom.
Panel row 2, column 1: Pantai, a tropical moonlit cove. Chunky curved palm trees framing edges, turquoise sea and small distant island, huge luminous moon, soft distant waves. Open warm ochre sandy foreground, smooth rocks and small shells only at far margins.
Panel row 2, column 2: Padang Garam, an ancient salt desert. Sculpted lavender buttes and rose quartz formations at the sides, indigo night sky with a pale moon. Open ivory salt-pan ground with a few broad polygonal cracks and soft violet shadows, calm and still.
Panel row 3, column 1: Langit Besi, a fantastical iron fortress foundry. Massive rounded bronze pipes, dark blue steel girders, riveted machinery, huge amber furnace glow at the back, brass fittings. Open dark teal metal-tile floor lit by orange reflected fire. Architecture rounded and toy-like with strong three-dimensional forms.
Panel row 3, column 2: Malam Panjang, surreal final dream realm. Floating sculpted obsidian monoliths at sides and a luminous lavender tear in the distant starry indigo sky, misty violet cosmic clouds. Open dark amethyst stone platform across bottom with subtle glowing cyan seams, soft reflections. Rich magical depth.
Constraints: EXACT six equal panels in the specified grid/order. No lettering, logos, watermarks, characters, foreground obstructions or composited game screenshots. Consistent miniature-scale prerendered 3D aesthetic across all panels.
